title: The camp's cancelled
goal: On the phone with Sēf, deal with a cancelled weekend camp booking and stop him cancelling everything else
tip: Some verbs have four consonants. kansal 'cancel', from English, works like a Form II verb: kansalt 'I cancelled', bakansil 'I'll cancel', la tkansil 'don't cancel'. Put t- in front for 'got cancelled': ir-riḥla tkansalat 'the trip's been called off'.
grammar: quadriliteral verbs: kansal 'cancel' (kansalt, ykansil, bakansil); tkansal 'got cancelled'
dialogue: A
سمعت؟ كنسلوا الحجز حق المخيم!
simaʿt? kansalaw il-ḥajz ḥagg il-mukhayyam!
Have you heard? They've cancelled the camp booking!
B
ليش كنسلوه؟ دفعنا كل شي!
lēsh kansalōh? difaʿna kill shay!
Why did they cancel it? We'd paid for everything!
A
يقولون عندهم مشكلة في المخيم، وبيرجعون لنا الفلوس كلها
ygūlūn ʿind-hum mushkila fi l-mukhayyam, w biyrajjʿūn-lna l-flūs killha
They say they've got a problem at the camp, and they'll give us all our money back.
B
يعني الرحلة تكنسلت؟ ما في أمل؟
yaʿni r-riḥla tkansalat? ma fī amal?
So the trip's off? No chance at all?
A
هيه. وأنا بعد كنسلت السيارة اللي حجزتها
hē. w ana baʿad kansalt is-sayyāra illi ḥajazt-ha
Yes. And I've cancelled the car I booked, too.
B
ليش؟ لا تكنسل كل شي! خلنا نروح مكان ثاني
lēsh? la tkansil kill shay! khallna nrūḥ makān thāni
Why? Don't cancel everything! Let's go somewhere else.
A
زين، بحجزها مرة ثانية. بس لا تكنسل انت في آخر لحظة!
zēn, baḥjizha marra thānya. bas la tkansil inta fi ākhir laḥẓa!
OK, I'll book it again. But don't you pull out at the last minute!
B
أنا؟ أبد! هالمرة ما بكنسل
ana? abad! hal-marra ma bakansil
Me? Never! This time I won't cancel.
A
إن شاء الله. كل شي ينحل! بكلم الشباب وبطرش لك المكان
in shāʼ allāh. kill shay yinḥall! bakallim ish-shabāb w baṭarrish-lak il-makān
Let's hope so. Everything can be sorted! I'll talk to the guys and send you the place.
items: I cancelled; you cancelled (to a man)
to a woman: kansalti (كنسلتي); he cancelled: kansal (كنسل); from English 'cancel'
a feminine thing: lēsh kansalōha? (ليش كنسلوها؟); they cancelled: kansalaw (كنسلوا)
a masculine thing: tkansal (تكنسل): il-mawʿid tkansal = the appointment's been cancelled
to a woman: la tkansilīn (لا تكنسلين)
booked: maḥjūz; I booked it (f.): ḥajazt-ha (حجزتها)
culture: Some English verbs have been part of Gulf speech for generations: chayyak 'check' was already written down in Kuwait in 1951. Newer ones take the same Arabic endings, like kansal 'cancel'. Mixing English into Arabic is most common among young people and in relaxed settings, so these verbs sound casual: with elders and in formal settings, people tend to use Arabic words.

title: Who messed up the file?
goal: At the office, tell Maryam the shared presentation has got messed up, and sort it out together
tip: kharbaṭ 'mess up' is a Gulf verb with four consonants: kharbaṭt 'I messed up', la tkharbiṭha 'don't mess it up'. With t- it happens by itself: il-alwān tkharbaṭat 'the colours got messed up'. The participle of tkharbaṭ starts with mi-: mitkharbiṭ 'messed up, in a muddle'.
grammar: quadriliteral verbs: kharbaṭ 'mess up', tkharbaṭ 'get messed up', mitkharbiṭ 'messed up'
dialogue: B
مريم، فتحتي العرض اليوم؟ كله متخربط!
Maryam, fataḥti l-ʿarẓ il-yōm? killah mitkharbiṭ!
Maryam, have you opened the presentation today? It's all messed up!
A
لا والله! شو صار له؟ أمس كان زين
la wallāh! shu ṣār-lah? ams kān zēn
Oh no! What's happened to it? It was fine yesterday.
B
الصور مب في مكانها، والألوان تخربطت بعد
iṣ-ṣuwar mub fi makānha, w il-alwān tkharbaṭat baʿad
The pictures aren't where they should be, and the colours have got messed up too.
A
يمكن حد فتحه من تلفونه وخربطه بدون ما يدري
yimkin ḥad fataḥah min tilifōnah w kharbaṭah bidūn ma yadri
Maybe someone opened it on their phone and messed it up without realising.
B
ممكن. لا تشيلين هم، عندي نسخة على اللابتوب
mumkin. la tshīlīn ham, ʿindi nuskha ʿala l-lābtōb
Could be. Don't worry, I've got a copy on my laptop.
A
الحمد لله! جهازي لعوزني اليوم، كل شوي يطفي
il-ḥamdu lillāh! jihāzi laʿwazni l-yōm, kill shwayy yiṭfi
Thank God! My computer's been driving me mad today, it keeps switching off.
B
وهذا بعد ما يرضى يشتغل… خلاص، اشتغل! طرشت لج النسخة
w hādha baʿad ma yirẓa yishtaghil… khalāṣ, ishtaghal! ṭarrasht-lich in-nuskha
And this one won't start either… there, it's on! I've sent you the copy.
A
ما شاء الله عليك! بشيك عليها قبل الاجتماع
mā shāʼ allāh ʿalēk! bachayyik ʿalēha gabil il-ijtimāʿ
Well done you! I'll check it before the meeting.
B
والسموحة… أنا اللي خربطت الألوان أمس!
w is-samūḥa… ana illi kharbaṭt il-alwān ams!
And sorry… I'm the one who messed up the colours yesterday!
A
مسموح! بس لا تخربطها مرة ثانية
masmūḥ! bas la tkharbiṭha marra thānya
Forgiven! But don't mess them up again.
items: messed up, in a mess (a masculine thing)
a feminine thing: mitkharbṭa (متخربطة); you'll also hear mlakhbaṭ (ملخبط)
it (f.) got messed up; they (things) got messed up
I'm the one who messed (it) up
you messed (it) up: kharbaṭt (خربطت) to a man, kharbaṭti (خربطتي) to a woman
don't mess it (f.) up (to a man)
to a woman: la tkharbṭīnha (لا تخربطينها); a masculine thing: la tkharbiṭah (لا تخربطه)
it won't start, it won't work (a masculine thing)
a feminine thing: ma tirẓa tishtaghil (ما ترضى تشتغل); yirẓa = he's willing, he agrees
(recognise) without realising (said of yourself): bidūn ma adri (بدون ما أدري)
it's been driving me mad, it's given me a hard time (UAE)
(recognise) I've had a rough time, I'm worn out: tlaʿwazt (تلعوزت)
it keeps switching off (a masculine thing)
(recognise) a feminine thing: kill shwayy tiṭfi (كل شوي تطفي)

title: Turn it off and on again
goal: Help Sēf when his phone freezes: restart it, then sort out the numbers he didn't save
tip: English verbs come in two ways. Some take Arabic endings, like Form II: sayyaf 'save' gives sayyaft 'I saved', lāzim tsayyif 'you have to save'. Others stay in English after sawwa 'do': basawwi abdēt 'I'll do an update', sawwēt-lah blōk 'I blocked him'.
grammar: English verbs: Arabic endings (sayyaf 'save') or sawwa + the English word (sawwi abdēt)
dialogue: A
يا ريّال، تلفوني معلق! الشاشة ما تتحرك
yā rayyāl, tilifōni mʿallag! ish-shāsha ma titḥarrak
Mate, my phone's frozen! The screen won't move.
B
عادي، صار لي نفس الشي. طفه وشغله
ʿādi, ṣār-li nafs ish-shay. ṭaffah w shaghghlah
Happens all the time, the same thing happened to me. Turn it off and on again.
A
حاولت، بس ما يرضى يطفي!
ḥāwalt, bas ma yirẓa yiṭfi!
I've tried, but it won't switch off!
B
عيل اضغط على الزر شوي، لين يطفي
ʿayal iẓghaṭ ʿala z-zirr shwayy, lēn yiṭfi
Then hold the button down for a bit, till it switches off.
A
زين… اشتغل! بس الأرقام اليديدة اللي ما سيفتها، ما ألقاها!
zēn… ishtaghal! bas il-argām il-yidīda illi ma sayyaft-ha, ma algāha!
OK… it's on! But the new numbers I hadn't saved, I can't find them!
B
كم مرة قلت لك؟ لازم تسيف كل رقم على طول
cham marra gilt-lak? lāzim tsayyif kill ragam ʿala ṭūl
How many times have I told you? You have to save every number straight away.
A
خلاص، من اليوم بسيف كل شي. وبسوي أبديت بعد
khalāṣ, min il-yōm basayyif kill shay. w basawwi abdēt baʿad
All right, from today I'll save everything. And I'll do an update, too.
B
زين. ورقمي؟ سيفته؟
zēn. w ragmi? sayyaftah?
Good. And my number? Did you save it?
A
رقمك؟ لا تخاف، رقمك محفوظ عندي من زمان!
ragmak? la tkhāf, ragmak maḥfūẓ ʿindi min zamān!
Your number? Don't worry, I've had your number saved for ages!
items: my phone's frozen, my phone's stuck
a feminine thing: ish-shāsha mʿallga (الشاشة معلقة) = the screen's frozen
turn it (m.) off and on again (to a man)
to a woman: ṭaffīh w shaghghlīh (طفيه وشغليه)
a feminine thing: lēn tiṭfi (لين تطفي)
I saved it (f.), I saved them (numbers, files); you saved it (to a man)
to a woman (you saved it): sayyaftīha (سيفتيها); a masculine thing: sayyaftah (سيفته); from English 'save'; you'll also hear khazzant-ha (خزنتها)
you have to save (it) (to a man)
to a woman: lāzim tsayyfīn (لازم تسيفين)
I'll do an update, I'll update (it)
you'll also hear it with p: apdēt
the same thing happened to me
to us: ṣār-lna nafs ish-shay (صار لنا نفس الشي)
press the button, hold the button (to a man)
to a woman: iẓghaṭi ʿala z-zirr (اضغطي على الزر)
culture: Tech talk among young people in the Gulf is full of English. Many English words simply go after sawwa 'do', so the Arabic verb carries the person and tense and the English word stays as it is: sawwēt abdēt 'I did an update', sawwa lāyk 'he liked it'. It's easy to build your own, but keep it for friends. With older people, use Arabic verbs where you can: ṭaffah w shaghghlah.

title: Did Sēf block me?
goal: Fahad thinks Sēf has blocked him; find out what really happened and keep him in the group chat
tip: Put the person after sawwa with l-: sawwā-li blōk 'he blocked me', sawwēt-lah blōk 'I blocked him', ysawwī-lak blōk 'he blocks you'. The English word never changes; only sawwa does: kint basawwī-lak blōk 'I was about to block you'.
grammar: sawwa + English word with a dative ending: sawwā-li blōk 'he blocked me'
dialogue: A
سيف سوى لي بلوك! رسايلي ما توصله
Sēf sawwā-li blōk! rasāyli ma tōṣlah
Sēf's blocked me! My messages aren't getting through to him.
B
سيف؟ مستحيل! يمكن غلطة
Sēf? mustaḥīl! yimkin ghalṭa
Sēf? No way! Maybe it's a mistake.
A
شنو غلطة؟ صار له يومين ما يرد علي، وصورته اختفت!
shinu ghalṭa? ṣār-lah yōmēn ma yrudd ʿalay, w ṣūrtah ikhtafat!
What do you mean, a mistake? He hasn't answered me for two days, and his picture's disappeared!
B
خلني أشيك… لا، حتى أنا ما يرد علي
khallni achayyik… la, ḥatta ana ma yrudd ʿalay
Let me check… no, he's not answering me either.
A
اسمع! سيف اتصل الحين. يقول غيّر رقمه ونسى يقول لنا
ismaʿ! Sēf ittaṣal il-ḥīn. ygūl ghayyar ragmah w nisa ygūl-lana
Listen! Sēf's just rung. He says he changed his number and forgot to tell us.
B
الحمد لله، مب بلوك! بس ليش يسوي لك بلوك أصلا؟
il-ḥamdu lillāh, mub blōk! bas lēsh ysawwī-lak blōk aṣlan?
Thank God it's not a block! But why would he block you anyway?
A
لأني طرشت فيديوهات وايد في القروب، والشباب حطوني ميوت
lanni ṭarrasht fīdyōhāt wāyid fi l-grūb, w ish-shabāb ḥaṭṭōni myūt
Because I sent loads of videos in the group, and the guys have put me on mute.
B
وأنا بعد كنت بسوي لك بلوك!
w ana baʿad kint basawwī-lak blōk!
And I was about to block you too!
A
حتى انت؟ خلاص، بطلع من القروب!
ḥatta inta? khalāṣ, baṭlaʿ min il-grūb!
You too? Right, I'm leaving the group!
B
لا تطلع! بس خفف الفيديوهات
la tiṭlaʿ! bas khaffif il-fīdyōhāt
Don't leave! Just cut down on the videos.
items: I blocked him: sawwēt-lah blōk (سويت له بلوك)
why would he block you? (to a man)
to a woman: lēsh ysawwī-lich blōk? (ليش يسوي لج بلوك؟)
they've put me on mute, they've muted me (Kuwait)
my messages aren't getting through to him
to her: rasāyli ma tōṣal-ha (رسايلي ما توصلها)
don't leave: la tiṭlaʿ (لا تطلع) to a man, la tiṭlaʿīn (لا تطلعين) to a woman
cut down on the videos (to a man)
to a woman: khaffifi l-fīdyōhāt (خففي الفيديوهات)

title: What do you hope for?
goal: In Bū Rāshid's majlis, talk about your hopes for after your studies and answer his good wishes
tip: atmanna 'I hope, I'd love to' takes a bare verb: atmanna alga shughul hni 'I hope to find a job here'. For someone else, use their verb, with or without inn: atmanna (innak) tigʿid 'I hope you stay'. kint atmanna is a wish that can't come true: kint atmanna agdar 'I wish I could'.
grammar: atmanna 'I hope, I wish' + verb, + inn; kint atmanna 'I wish (but can't)'
dialogue: A
هلا والله بسالم! شو أخبار الدراسة؟
hala wallāh b-Sālim! shu akhbār id-dirāsa?
Welcome, Sālim! How are your studies going?
B
هلا فيك يا عمي. باقي لي سنة وأخلص، إن شاء الله
hala fīk yā ʿammi. bāgi-li sana w akhalliṣ, in shāʼ allāh
Hello, uncle. I've got one year left and then I'm done, God willing.
A
ما شاء الله! وبعدين؟ بترجع لندن ولّا بتقعد عندنا؟
mā shāʼ allāh! w baʿdēn? bitirjaʿ Landan walla bitigʿid ʿindana?
Wonderful! And then? Will you go back to London or stay with us?
B
أتمنى ألقى شغل هني. دبي صارت مثل ديرتي
atmanna alga shughul hni. Dbayy ṣārat mithil dīrti
I hope to find a job here. Dubai's become like home to me.
A
الله يوفقك. وأتمنى إنك تقعد، الكل يحبك هني
allāh ywaffgak. w atmanna innak tigʿid, il-kill yḥibbak hni
God grant you success. And I hope you stay; everyone here loves you.
B
آمين. تسلم يا عمي. بس أهلي يتمنون أرجع
āmīn. tislam yā ʿammi. bas ahli yitmannūn arjaʿ
Amen. Thank you, uncle. But my family are hoping I'll go back.
A
الله يسلمك. طبيعي، كل أم تتمنى ولدها يكون يمها
allāh ysallmak. ṭabīʿi, kill umm titmanna wildha ykūn yammha
God keep you. That's natural; every mother wants her son near her.
B
صح. كنت أتمنى أقدر أعيش في المكانين!
ṣaḥḥ. kint atmanna agdar aʿīsh fi l-makānēn!
True. I wish I could live in both places!
A
إن شاء الله يصير اللي تتمناه، وتلقى الشغل اللي تبيه
in shāʼ allāh yṣīr illi titmannāh, w tilga sh-shughul illi tabīh
God willing, what you wish for will happen, and you'll find the job you want.
items: I hope, I wish; I'd love to (+ verb)
a woman says the same; you hope: titmanna (تتمنى) to a man, titmannīn (تتمنين) to a woman
to a woman: atmanna innich (أتمنى إنج); I hope he…: atmanna innah (أتمنى إنه)
I wish, I'd have loved (to) (but it can't happen)
I hope to find a job, I hope I find work
it's (f.) become like home to me, it feels like my own country (a city)
dīra = home country, homeland; a masculine place: ṣār mithil dīrti (صار مثل ديرتي)
(recognise) to a woman: il-kill yḥibbich (الكل يحبج)
every mother wishes, every mother wants
what you wish for, what you hope for (to a man)
(recognise) to a woman: illi titmannīnah (اللي تتمنينه)
culture: Older people often answer a young man's plans with a blessing. allāh ywaffgak 'God grant you success' is answered with āmīn, and a thank-you with tislam gets allāh ysallmak.
task: This week: with a tutor or exchange partner (search a tutoring site for «Emirati Arabic tutor» or «مدرس لهجة إماراتية»), talk for 10 minutes about your plans after your studies. Say two things you hope for with atmanna, one thing you wish you could do with kint atmanna, and ask them what they hope for (titmanna?).

title: I wish I'd come
goal: Sēf shows you photos of the trip you missed; say what you wish had happened and what you hope for next time
tip: yā rēt 'I wish, if only' (you know yā lēt too) can take a pronoun: yā rētni 'I wish I…'. A past verb after it is a regret: yā rētni riḥt 'I wish I'd gone'. A present verb is a hope: yā rēt il-jaww yiẓall ḥilu 'I hope the weather stays nice'.
grammar: yā rēt, yā rētni + past (regret) or present (hope); yā rēt lō … chān
dialogue: A
شوف الصور! هذا الوادي اللي رحنا له في حتا
shūf iṣ-ṣuwar! hādha l-wādi illi riḥnā-lah fi Ḥatta
Look at the photos! This is the wadi we went to in Hatta.
B
ما شاء الله! يا ريتني رحت وياكم
mā shāʼ allāh! yā rētni riḥt wiyyākum
Wow! I wish I'd gone with you.
A
يا ريت! بس انت كنسلت في آخر لحظة
yā rēt! bas inta kansalt fi ākhir laḥẓa
If only! But you pulled out at the last minute.
B
كان عندي امتحان. لو ما كان عندي، جان ييت
kān ʿindi imtiḥān. lō ma kān ʿindi, chān yīt
I had an exam. If I hadn't had one, I'd have come.
A
يا ريت لو قلت لي من قبل، جان غيرنا الموعد
yā rēt lō gilt-li min gabil, chān ghayyarna l-mawʿid
If only you'd told me before, we'd have changed the date.
B
صح. يا ريتني فكرت جي
ṣaḥḥ. yā rētni fakkart chī
True. I wish I'd thought of it like that.
A
عادي. المرة الياية بنروح كلنا، ويا ريت الجو يظل حلو
ʿādi. il-marra l-yāya binrūḥ killna, w yā rēt il-jaww yiẓall ḥilu
Never mind. Next time we'll all go, and I hope the weather stays nice.
B
يا ريت! وهالمرة ما بكنسل
yā rēt! w hal-marra ma bakansil
I hope so! And this time I won't cancel.
A
وإذا كنسلت، بحط صورتك في القروب!
w idha kansalt, baḥuṭṭ ṣūrtak fi l-grūb!
And if you cancel, I'll post your photo in the group so everyone knows!
items: I wish, if only; I hope so
you'll see written ياريت; it means the same as yā lēt (يا ليت)
I wish I'd gone with you (all)
with you (one man): wiyyāk (وياك); you'll see written ياريتني
the result takes chān: yā rēt lō gilt-li, chān ghayyarna l-mawʿid = if only you'd told me, we'd have changed the date; you'll see written ياريت لو
I wish I'd thought of it like that
(recognise) a feminine thing: tiẓall ḥilwa (تظل حلوة)
I'll put (up) your picture (to a man)
to a woman: baḥuṭṭ ṣūrtich (بحط صورتج)

title: Which do you prefer?
goal: At the office, Maryam is planning the team lunch; say what you prefer, and when you don't mind
tip: afaẓẓil 'I prefer, I'd rather' takes a noun or a bare verb: afaẓẓil niṭlub 'I'd rather we ordered in'. Compare with ʿala: afaẓẓil il-ʿarabi ʿala l-hindi. To a woman, 'what do you prefer?' is shu tfaẓẓlīn? To a man it's shu tfaẓẓil?
grammar: afaẓẓil 'I prefer' + noun or verb; afaẓẓil X ʿala Y; badāl ma 'instead of'
dialogue: A
بنسوي غدا للفريق يوم الخميس. نروح مطعم ولّا نطلب للمكتب؟
binsawwi ghada lil-farīg yōm il-khamīs. nrūḥ maṭʿam walla niṭlub lil-maktab?
We're doing a team lunch on Thursday. Shall we go to a restaurant or order in to the office?
B
أنا أفضل نطلب. المطاعم زحمة وقت الغدا
ana afaẓẓil niṭlub. il-maṭāʿim zaḥma wagt il-ghada
I'd rather we ordered in. Restaurants are packed at lunchtime.
A
زين. وشو تفضل، عربي ولّا هندي؟
zēn. w shu tfaẓẓil, ʿarabi walla hindi?
OK. And what do you prefer, Arabic or Indian?
B
عادي عندي. وانتي شو تفضلين؟
ʿādi ʿindi. w inti shu tfaẓẓlīn?
I don't mind. And what do you prefer?
A
أنا أفضل العربي على الهندي، والمدير أصلا ما يحب الأكل الحار
ana afaẓẓil il-ʿarabi ʿala l-hindi, w il-mudīr aṣlan ma yḥibb il-akil il-ḥārr
I prefer Arabic to Indian, and the manager doesn't like spicy food anyway.
B
عيل خلنا نطلب عربي، بدال ما نطلب شي حار
ʿayal khallna niṭlub ʿarabi, badāl ma niṭlub shay ḥārr
Then let's order Arabic, instead of getting something spicy.
A
فكرة حلوة. والوقت؟ الساعة وحدة ولّا ثنتين؟
fikra ḥilwa. w il-wagt? is-sāʿa waḥda walla thintēn?
Good idea. And the time? One o'clock or two?
B
اللي يريحج. بس أفضل وحدة، بدال ما نقعد يوعانين
illi yrīḥich. bas afaẓẓil waḥda, badāl ma nigʿid yōʿānīn
Whatever suits you. But I'd rather one, instead of sitting around hungry.
A
خلاص، الساعة وحدة. بطرش للفريق الحين
khalāṣ, is-sāʿa waḥda. baṭarrish lil-farīg il-ḥīn
Done, one o'clock. I'll message the team now.
items: a woman says the same; afaẓẓil niṭlub = I'd rather we ordered (in)
what do you prefer? (to a woman)
to a man: shu tfaẓẓil? (شو تفضل؟), spelled like tfaẓẓal 'go ahead'
afaẓẓil il-gahwa ʿala l-karak = I prefer coffee to karak
I don't mind, it's all the same to me
whatever suits you, whatever's easiest for you (to a woman)
to a man: illi yrīḥak (اللي يريحك)
badāl ma nigʿid = instead of sitting (around)
we order in, we have it delivered to the office
(recognise) I don't like spicy food: ma aḥibb il-akil il-ḥārr (ما أحب الأكل الحار)
at dinner time: wagt il-ʿasha (وقت العشا)
culture: When a colleague asks what you'd prefer, ʿādi ʿindi 'I don't mind' or illi yrīḥich 'whatever suits you' is polite. But if you do have a preference, give it with a reason, as B does here: it helps the person who's organising.

title: I'm dying to see her
goal: Chat with Sēf about missing your family and what you're longing for, and hear about his mother's invitation
tip: For a strong want, say khāṭri 'I'm dying to, I long to' + a verb (khāṭri ashūf ummi) or fi + a thing (khāṭri fi hash-shay). For food you crave, say mishtahi (a woman: mishtahya). widdi lō is 'I'd love it if': widdi lō tiyi. All are warmer than abi.
grammar: strong wants: khāṭri + verb or fi; mishtahi; widdi lō; recycle: widdi, ḥabbēt
dialogue: A
شفيك ساكت؟ مشتاق لأهلك؟
shfīk sākit? mishtāg l-ahlak?
Why so quiet? Missing your family?
B
هيه والله. خاطري أشوف أمي
hē wallāh. khāṭri ashūf ummi
Yes, honestly. I'm dying to see my mum.
A
طبيعي. صار لك وايد ما رحت لندن؟
ṭabīʿi. ṣār-lak wāyid ma riḥt Landan?
That's natural. Has it been long since you went to London?
B
شهرين بس، وأحسها سنة كاملة. ومشتهي أكل أمي بعد
shahrēn bas, w aḥiss-ha sana kāmla. w mishtahi akil ummi baʿad
Only two months, and it feels like a whole year. And I'm craving my mum's cooking, too.
A
شو تطبخ لك أمك؟
shu tiṭbakh-lak ummak?
What does your mum cook for you?
B
روست يوم الأحد! ودي لو تيي دبي وتطبخ لنا
rōst yōm il-aḥad! widdi lō tiyi Dbayy w tiṭbakh-lna
A Sunday roast! I'd love it if she came to Dubai and cooked for us.
A
ليش لا؟ حبيت أقول لك: أمي تبي تعزم أهلك إذا يوا
lēsh la? ḥabbēt agūl-lak: ummi tabi tʿazim ahlak idha yaw
Why not? I wanted to tell you: my mum wants to invite your family if they come.
B
والله؟ من زمان خاطري في هالشي!
wallāh? min zamān khāṭri fi hash-shay!
Really? I've wanted that for ages!
A
خلاص، كلمهم. وأنا خاطري أذوق هالروست!
khalāṣ, kallimhum. w ana khāṭri adhūg har-rōst!
Done, talk to them. And I'm dying to taste this roast!
items: I'm dying to see, I long to see
a woman says the same; khāṭri + any verb: khāṭri asāfir = I'm dying to travel
I'd really love, I'm dying for (a thing)
khāṭri fi gahwa = I'm dying for a coffee
craving, I really fancy (food) (said by a man)
widdi lō tiyi = I'd love it if you came (to a man); you know widdi + verb 'I'd love to'
a whole month: shahar kāmil (شهر كامل)
my mum's cooking, my mum's food
your mum's cooking: akil ummak (to a man), akil ummich (to a woman)
she cooks for us; you cook for us (to a man)
to a woman (you cook for us): tiṭbakhīn-lna (تطبخين لنا); she cooks for you: tiṭbakh-lak (تطبخ لك)
has it been long since you went (to)…? (to a man)
هل مضى وقت طويل منذ ذهبت…؟
(recognise) to a woman: ṣār-lich wāyid ma riḥti…? (صار لج وايد ما رحتي…؟)

title: Checkpoint 4.2: getting ready for your family
goal: Checkpoint: with Sēf, plan your family's visit: what they'd like, who's coming, and what you'd all prefer to do
tip: Review of s4u016–028, now about other people: il-akil il-imārāti 'Emirati food', idha ma kansal 'if he doesn't cancel', yitmanna yshūf 'he's hoping to see', plus nisēt aruddah, ʿaṭētni iyyāh and widdi lō. ʿala l-ʿasha here is 'for dinner'.
grammar: checkpoint 4.2: iyyā-, kansal, atmanna, yā rēt, afaẓẓil, khāṭri, widdi lō, with 'they' and 'he'
dialogue: A
أهلك بيوصلون الخميس؟ أمي تسأل شو يفضلون على العشا
ahlak biyōṣlūn il-khamīs? ummi tisʼal shu yfaẓẓlūn ʿala l-ʿasha
Is your family arriving on Thursday? My mum's asking what they'd like for dinner.
B
هيه، إن شاء الله. خاطرهم في الأكل الإماراتي
hē, in shāʼ allāh. khāṭirhum fi l-akil il-imārāti
Yes, God willing. They're dying to try Emirati food.
A
زين! وهذا شاحنك، عطيتني إياه السبت ونسيت أرده
zēn! w hādha shāḥnak, ʿaṭētni iyyāh is-sabt w nisēt aruddah
Great! And here's your charger: you gave it to me on Saturday and I forgot to give it back.
B
ما عليه. يا ريت كل الناس يردون الأغراض مثلك!
ma ʿalēh. yā rēt kill in-nās yruddūn il-aghrāẓ mithlak!
Never mind. I wish everyone gave things back like you!
A
وفهد ياي بعد، إذا ما كنسل مثل كل مرة
w Fahad yāy baʿad, idha ma kansal mithil kill marra
And Fahad's coming too, if he doesn't cancel like every time.
B
لا، هالمرة كلمني. يقول يتمنى يشوف أبوي
la, hal-marra kallamni. ygūl yitmanna yshūf ubūy
No, this time he rang me. He says he's hoping to meet my dad.
A
حلو! وانت شو تفضل، نقعد في البيت ولّا نطلع البر؟
ḥilu! w inta shu tfaẓẓil, nigʿid fi l-bēt walla niṭlaʿ il-barr?
Nice! And what would you prefer, stay at home or go out to the desert?
B
أفضل البيت أول يوم. أكيد بيكونون تعبانين
afaẓẓil il-bēt awwal yōm. akīd biykūnūn taʿbānīn
I'd rather home on the first day. They're bound to be tired.
A
صح. أتمنى إنهم يستانسون هني
ṣaḥḥ. atmanna innhum yistānsūn hni
True. I hope they have a lovely time here.
B
إن شاء الله. ودي لو يحبون دبي مثلي
in shāʼ allāh. widdi lō yḥibbūn Dbayy mithli
God willing. I'd love it if they loved Dubai as much as I do.
items: I forgot to give it (m.) back
a feminine thing: nisēt arudd-ha (نسيت أردها)
Kuwaiti food: il-akil il-kwēti (الأكل الكويتي); they're dying for: khāṭirhum fi (خاطرهم في)
yā rēt kill in-nās mithlak = I wish everyone were like you (to a man)
if they don't cancel: idha ma kansalaw (إذا ما كنسلوا)
he's hoping to see, he'd love to meet
she's hoping to see: titmanna tshūf (تتمنى تشوف)
he gives things back: yrudd il-aghrāẓ (يرد الأغراض)
